discrepancies.summary: Tabbycat setting has no CrabbyTab equivalent: scoring__teamscore_includes_ghosts (the DebateXML importer totals ballots with CrabbyTab's default, false; Tabbycat's default is true; the harness recomputes the totals)
discrepancies.note: CrabbyTab's DebateXML importer totals each imported ballot with CrabbyTab's defaults, so iron-person (ghost) speeches are left out of team scores. Tabbycat's default, and WUDC 35.9.3.2, is to include them, and Tabbycat's importer applies the style preset first. The harness recomputes the imported totals with Tabbycat's setting so every later comparison starts from equal team scores. Follow-up: have the importer apply the style's preset (RULES_PRESETS) before totalling ballots.

Adjudicator-team history is a soft penalty in both engines (Tabbycat's adj_history_penalty, mapped to CrabbyTab's adjHistoryPenalty). Neither allocation breaks a hard constraint and chair quality is within the 10% band. CrabbyTab's allocation has one more repeat in both voting fixtures, which is worth watching but is not a rule violation.

discrepancies.summary: teams: "draw_strength" differs for 98 row(s), first after round 1
discrepancies.note: In BP, Tabbycat's draw strength sums opponents' points; CrabbyTab's draw_strength_wins counts opponents' wins (a 1st or 2nd). The BP rules preset already lists this as unsupported and leaves draw strength out of the BP precedence (src/lib/setup/presets.ts), so BP ranks still agree. Follow-up: compute BP draw strength from points.

discrepancies.summary: teams: "wins" differs for 76 row(s), first after round 1
discrepancies.note: Tabbycat records no wins in BP preliminary rounds (0 for every team); CrabbyTab counts a 1st or 2nd as a win. 'wins' is not in any BP precedence, but it feeds the draw-strength difference above.

Before any results every team is tied, and neither engine picks round-1 byes at random. Tabbycat's random draw manager takes the last teams in database order (the last imported); CrabbyTab's lowest_ranked rule keeps list order, so the first teams always sit out. Both are arbitrary, fixed preferences; AGENTS.md section 7.2 asks for an explicit random tie-break. Follow-up: break the bye tie with the draw's seeded RNG.

discrepancies.summary: Round 5: only CrabbyTab refused to draw

crabbytab.error: No side assignment for University A A vs University D B satisfies the configured side limits (at most 3 times per side).

discrepancies.note: With max 3 debates per side, T13 and T19 have both been affirmative three times and fold pairs them together. CrabbyTab pairs first and checks side limits afterwards (sideAllocator.ts), so it refuses the draw in 7 of 8 seeds even though valid pairings exist within the bracket. Tabbycat enforces the cap only in its min-cost ('graph') conflict avoidance (draw/generator/graph.py, which also checks t1_negs twice instead of t2_negs), so with one-up-one-down it draws and silently gives one of them a fourth affirmative. Follow-up: treat the side cap as a pairing constraint for fold and one-up-one-down.

discrepancies.summary: Break BC1: breaking teams differ (CrabbyTab holds 8 tied teams for 1 place(s) out for the tab director)
discrepancies.note: Eight teams are tied on wins for the last of six places. Tabbycat 2.12.1 breaks one of them, picked by its random standings tie-break, and marks the other seven as reserves. Its code says every team tied for the last place should break, but add_reserve_teams then overwrites them as reserves (breakqual/base.py). CrabbyTab holds the whole tie out of the break and blocks generation until the tab director resolves it, so it breaks five teams and reports the tie.
Same tie as above: Tabbycat lists the seven tied teams it did not break as reserves. CrabbyTab picks no reserves until the break cutoff tie is resolved.

discrepancies.summary: Break BC1: break ranks (seeds) differ for teams both engines break
discrepancies.note: T5, T8, T11 and T18 are tied (3 wins, the only metric). Tabbycat gives them the same break rank (2); CrabbyTab numbers them 2 to 5 in standings order, which is team-name order inside a tie, so elimination seeding among tied teams is decided by name and the tie is not shown. Follow-up: carry equal seeds into elimination pairing or mark the tie.
